claim: Changes in chondrocyte gene expression can contribute to the development of osteoarthritis (OA).
source: Changes in chondrocyte gene expression can contribute to the development of osteoarthritis (OA), and so recognition of the regulative processes during chondrogenesis can lead to a better understanding of OA.
evidence: This is a general statement about OA pathogenesis that draws from established scientific understanding in the field.

claim: microRNAs (miRNAs) are key regulators of gene expression in chondrocytes/OA.
source: microRNAs (miRNAs) are key regulators of gene expression in chondrocytes/OA, and we have used a combined experimental, bioinformatic, and systems biology approach to explore the multiple miRNA–mRNA interactions that regulate chondrogenesis.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific knowledge about miRNA function in chondrocytes and OA.

claim: A longitudinal chondrogenesis bioinformatic analysis identified paralogues miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p as pro-chondrogenic regulators.
source: A longitudinal chondrogenesis bioinformatic analysis identified paralogues miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p as pro-chondrogenic regulators.
evidence: This claim is supported by the bioinformatic analysis described in the manuscript using TimiRGeN.

claim: Alteration of miR-199a-5p or miR-199b-5p expression led to significant inverse modulation of key chondrogenic genes and extracellular matrix production.
source: Experimental work in human cells demonstrated alteration of miR-199a-5p or miR-199b-5p expression led to significant inverse modulation of key chondrogenic genes and extracellular matrix production.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 demonstrating changes in ACAN, COL2A1, SOX9, and GAG levels.

claim: miR-199a/b-5p targets FZD6, ITGA3 and CAV1 were identified by inhibition experiments.
source: miR-199a/b-5p targets FZD6, ITGA3 and CAV1 were identified by inhibition experiments and verified as direct targets by luciferase assay.
evidence: This is supported by RNAseq data (Figure 3) and inhibition experiments (Figure 4A).

claim: FZD6, ITGA3 and CAV1 were verified as direct targets of miR-199a/b-5p by luciferase assay.
source: miR-199a/b-5p targets FZD6, ITGA3 and CAV1 were identified by inhibition experiments and verified as direct targets by luciferase assay.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: This is the first multi-miRNA model of a chondrogenesis-based system.
source: This is the first multi-miRNA model of a chondrogenesis-based system, and highlights the complex relationships between regulatory miRNAs, and their target mRNAs.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the work, which is a statement of fact about the literature.

claim: Differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) into chondrocytes occurs by the process of chondrogenesis.
source: Differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) into chondrocytes occurs by the process of chondrogenesis (Bosnakovski et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bosnakovski et al., 2006.

claim: Chondrogenesis is an important process during development as it is a pre-requisite for skeletogenesis.
source: This is an important process during development as it is a pre-requisite for skeletogenesis.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about developmental biology.

claim: Chondrocytes perform the vital role of generating cartilage during embryogenesis.
source: Chondrocytes perform the vital role of generating cartilage during embryogenesis, but also maintain cartilage throughout life, including at the ends of long bones in articulating joints (Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015.

claim: Chondrocytes maintain cartilage throughout life, including at the ends of long bones in articulating joints.
source: Chondrocytes perform the vital role of generating cartilage during embryogenesis, but also maintain cartilage throughout life, including at the ends of long bones in articulating joints (Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015.

claim: The master transcription factor responsible for chondrogenesis is SOX9.
source: The master transcription factor responsible for chondrogenesis is SOX9 and during this process chondrocytes secrete anabolic proteins such as type II collagen and aggrecan, encoded by COL2A1 and ACAN, which constitute a significant functional portion of the cartilaginous extracellular matrix (ECM) (Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015; Hoshi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015 and Hoshi et al., 2017.

claim: During chondrogenesis chondrocytes secrete anabolic proteins such as type II collagen and aggrecan, encoded by COL2A1 and ACAN.
source: The master transcription factor responsible for chondrogenesis is SOX9 and during this process chondrocytes secrete anabolic proteins such as type II collagen and aggrecan, encoded by COL2A1 and ACAN, which constitute a significant functional portion of the cartilaginous extracellular matrix (ECM) (Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015; Hoshi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015 and Hoshi et al., 2017.

claim: Type II collagen and aggrecan constitute a significant functional portion of the cartilaginous extracellular matrix (ECM).
source: The master transcription factor responsible for chondrogenesis is SOX9 and during this process chondrocytes secrete anabolic proteins such as type II collagen and aggrecan, encoded by COL2A1 and ACAN, which constitute a significant functional portion of the cartilaginous extracellular matrix (ECM) (Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015; Hoshi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Akkiraju and Nohe, 2015 and Hoshi et al., 2017.

claim: With increasing age and influenced by a mixture of factors such as (epi)genetics, obesity, and mechanical injury/stress, chondrocytes will increasingly express catabolic proteins such as matrix metalloproteinases which degrade the cartilage ECM.
source: With increasing age and influenced by a mixture of factors such as (epi)genetics, obesity, and mechanical injury/stress, chondrocytes will increasingly express catabolic proteins such as matrix metalloproteinases which degrade the cartilage ECM (Hoshi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hoshi et al., 2017.

claim: The chronic loss of cartilage contributes to the extremely debilitating condition osteoarthritis (OA).
source: Ultimately the chronic loss of cartilage contributes to the extremely debilitating condition osteoarthritis (OA), which remains incurable with treatment options limited to pain relief medication and end-stage joint replacement surgery (Grässel and Muschter, 2020; Loeser et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Grässel and Muschter, 2020 and Loeser et al., 2012.

claim: Osteoarthritis remains incurable with treatment options limited to pain relief medication and end-stage joint replacement surgery.
source: Ultimately the chronic loss of cartilage contributes to the extremely debilitating condition osteoarthritis (OA), which remains incurable with treatment options limited to pain relief medication and end-stage joint replacement surgery (Grässel and Muschter, 2020; Loeser et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Grässel and Muschter, 2020 and Loeser et al., 2012.

claim: miRNAs are short non-coding RNAs – roughly 19-22 nt long that negatively regulate target mRNAs.
source: miRNAs are short non-coding RNAs – roughly 19-22 nt long that negatively regulate target mRNAs (Bartel, 2009; Sevignani et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bartel, 2009 and Sevignani et al., 2006.

claim: Mammalian miRNA–mRNA interactions occur via complementary sequence specificity between a 7 and 8 nt stretch of the miRNA known as the seed sequence, and positions along the 3′UTR of the target mRNA.
source: Mammalian miRNA–mRNA interactions occur via complementary sequence specificity between a 7 and 8 nt stretch of the miRNA known as the seed sequence, and positions along the 3′UTR of the target mRNA (Lai, 2002; Doench and Sharp, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lai, 2002 and Doench and Sharp, 2004.

claim: miRNA–mRNA interactions are complex because a single mRNA can be targeted by many miRNAs, and a single miRNA can target many mRNAs.
source: miRNA–mRNA interactions are complex because a single mRNA can be targeted by many miRNAs, and a single miRNA can target many mRNAs.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about miRNA biology.

claim: Previous work identified significantly altered miRNAs during chondrogenesis and demonstrated the role of miR-140 in regulating chondrocyte gene expression.
source: Our previous work identified significantly altered miRNAs during chondrogenesis and demonstrated the role of miR-140 in regulating chondrocyte gene expression (Barter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Barter et al., 2015.

claim: miR-140 has emerged as a vital regulator of chondrogenesis, cartilage, and OA.
source: miR-140 has emerged as a vital regulator of chondrogenesis, cartilage, and OA, and have been hypothesized as effective drug targets due to their pro-chondrogenic regulation (Miyaki et al., 2009; Katoh et al., 2021; Swingler et al., 2012; Karlsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Miyaki et al., 2009; Katoh et al., 2021; Swingler et al., 2012; Karlsen et al., 2016.

claim: miR-140 has been hypothesized as effective drug targets due to their pro-chondrogenic regulation.
source: miR-140 has emerged as a vital regulator of chondrogenesis, cartilage, and OA, and have been hypothesized as effective drug targets due to their pro-chondrogenic regulation (Miyaki et al., 2009; Katoh et al., 2021; Swingler et al., 2012; Karlsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Miyaki et al., 2009; Katoh et al., 2021; Swingler et al., 2012; Karlsen et al., 2016.

claim: miR-455 has been shown to be important regulators in maintaining healthy cartilage and protecting against OA development.
source: Additional miRNAs, such as miR-455, have also been shown to be important regulators in maintaining healthy cartilage and protecting against OA development (Hu et al., 2019; Ito et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hu et al., 2019 and Ito et al., 2021.

claim: Eight signalling pathways were found enriched in at least three of the five timepoints during chondrogenesis.
source: Eight signalling pathways were found enriched in at least three of the five timepoints (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the TimiRGeN analysis and shown in Figure 1.

claim: miR-140-5p was the most positively changing miRNA in seven pathways: adipogenesis, clear cell renal cell carcinoma pathways (CCRCCP), epidermal growth factor/epidermal growth factor receptor (EGF/EGFR), endochondral ossification, endochondral ossification with skeletal dysplasia (EOSD), gastrin signalling pathway, and vascular endothelial growth factor-A/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 signalling pathway (VEGFA-VEGFR2).
source: miR-140-5p was the most positively changing miRNA in the following seven pathways: adipogenesis, clear cell renal cell carcinoma pathways (CCRCCP), epidermal growth factor/epidermal growth factor receptor (EGF/EGFR), endochondral ossification, endochondral ossification with skeletal dysplasia (EOSD), gastrin signalling pathway, and vascular endothelial growth factor-A/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 signalling pathway (VEGFA-VEGFR2).
evidence: This is based on the TimiRGeN analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: miR-199b-5p was the second most positively changing microRNA in six pathways: CCRCCP, EGF/EGFR, endochondral ossification, EOSD, gastrin signalling pathway, and VEGFA-VEGFR2.
source: miR-199b-5p was the second most positively changing microRNA in the following six pathways: CCRCCP, EGF/EGFR, endochondral ossification, EOSD, gastrin signalling pathway, and VEGFA-VEGFR2.
evidence: This is based on the TimiRGeN analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Significant upregulation was seen in ACAN, COL2A1, and GAG (DMB) levels following miR-199a-5p overexpression.
source: Significant upregulation was seen in ACAN, COL2A1, and GAG (DMB) levels following miR-199a-5p overexpression (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: When miR-199a-5p expression was inhibited ACAN, COL2A1, and SOX9 were significantly downregulated at multiple timepoints.
source: In contrast, when miR-199a-5p expression was inhibited ACAN, COL2A1, and SOX9 were significantly downregulated at multiple timepoints (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GAG levels were significantly decreased, by ~40%, at day 7 following miR-199a-5p inhibition.
source: GAG levels were also significantly decreased, by ~40%, at day 7.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: When miR-199b-5p was inhibited, significant downregulation of ACAN, COL2A1, and GAG levels occurred.
source: When miR-199b-5p was inhibited, similar significant downregulation of ACAN, COL2A1, and GAG levels occurred (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Inhibition of miR-199a-5p and -199b-5p together caused a more consistent reduction of ACAN, COL2A1, and SOX9 expression.
source: Inhibition of miR-199a-5p and -199b-5p together caused a more consistent reduction of ACAN, COL2A1, and SOX9 expression.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Positively changing genes during early chondrogenesis included COL2A1 (log2fc = 11.6), ACAN (log2fc = 9.18), and SOX9 (log2fc = 3.37).
source: Positively changing genes included COL2A1 (log2fc = 11.6), ACAN (log2fc = 9.18), and SOX9 (log2fc = 3.37).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis.

claim: Gene Ontology (GO) term analysis on the upregulated genes confirmed that the cells were differentiating towards chondrocytes with terms such as skeletal system development, ECM organisation, and regulation of cartilage development significantly enriched.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) term analysis on the upregulated genes confirmed that the cells were differentiating towards chondrocytes with terms such as skeletal system development, ECM organisation, and regulation of cartilage development significantly (adjusted p-values<0.05) enriched (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is based on GO term analysis of RNAseq data.

claim: Inhibition of miR-199a-5p resulted in 87 significantly differentially expressed genes at day 0.
source: To identify miR-199-regulated genes, undifferentiated control MSC samples were contrasted against undifferentiated MSCs with either miR-199a-5p or miR-199b-5p inhibition, which respectively resulted in 87 and 46 significantly DEGs (adjusted p-values<0.05) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis.

claim: Inhibition of miR-199b-5p resulted in 46 significantly differentially expressed genes at day 0.
source: To identify miR-199-regulated genes, undifferentiated control MSC samples were contrasted against undifferentiated MSCs with either miR-199a-5p or miR-199b-5p inhibition, which respectively resulted in 87 and 46 significantly DEGs (adjusted p-values<0.05) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis.

claim: Inhibition of miR-199a-5p resulted in 674 significantly differentially expressed genes at day 1 of chondrogenesis.
source: Similar comparisons at day 1 of chondrogenesis revealed inhibition of miR-199a-5p or miR-199b-5p respectively resulted in 674 and 817 DEGs.
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis.

claim: Inhibition of miR-199b-5p resulted in 817 significantly differentially expressed genes at day 1 of chondrogenesis.
source: Similar comparisons at day 1 of chondrogenesis revealed inhibition of miR-199a-5p or miR-199b-5p respectively resulted in 674 and 817 DEGs.
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis.

claim: 25 genes intersected between day 0 and day 1 chondrogenesis miR-199a-5p inhibition experiments.
source: Here, 25 and 341 genes intersected between day 0 and day 1 chondrogenesis inhibition experiments, indicating that both microRNAs may share functional repertoire of targets (chi-square observed vs. expected day 0 = 0.003477, day 1 = 0.000624).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis and chi-square test.

claim: 341 genes intersected between day 0 and day 1 chondrogenesis miR-199b-5p inhibition experiments.
source: Here, 25 and 341 genes intersected between day 0 and day 1 chondrogenesis inhibition experiments, indicating that both microRNAs may share functional repertoire of targets (chi-square observed vs. expected day 0 = 0.003477, day 1 = 0.000624).
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis and chi-square test.

claim: Both miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p may share functional repertoire of targets.
source: Here, 25 and 341 genes intersected between day 0 and day 1 chondrogenesis inhibition experiments, indicating that both microRNAs may share functional repertoire of targets (chi-square observed vs. expected day 0 = 0.003477, day 1 = 0.000624).
evidence: This is inferred from the overlap of differentially expressed genes and supported by chi-square statistical test.

claim: COL2A1, ACAN, and SOX9 were significantly lower in expression in day 1 samples after miR-199 inhibition.
source: COL2A1, ACAN, and SOX9 were significantly lower in expression in day 1 samples after miR-199 inhibition, validating the negative impact on chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is based on RNAseq differential expression analysis.

claim: Several terms associated with chondrogenesis were suppressed/less activated during day 1 analyses, including ECM constituents, skeletal system morphogenesis, ECM, and collagen containing ECM.
source: Interestingly several terms associated with chondrogenesis were suppressed/less activated during day 1 analyses, including ECM constituents, skeletal system morphogenesis, ECM, and collagen containing ECM.
evidence: This is based on GO term analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Twenty-one potential mRNA targets were predicted to be targeted by both miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p.
source: Twenty-one potential mRNA targets were predicted to be targeted by both miRNAs, and in alphabetical order they were ABHD17C, ATP13A2, CAV1, CTSL, DDR1, FZD6, GIT1, HIF1A, HK2, HSPA5, ITGA3, M6PR, MYH9, NECTIN2, NINL, PDE4D, PLXND1, PXN, SLC35A3, SLC35D1, VPS26A.
evidence: This is based on miRNAtap prediction analysis of RNAseq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Many of genes found through bioinformatic analysis were significantly downregulated during chondrogenesis in multiple studies, including CAV1, FZD6, ITGA3, and MYH9.
source: The tables showed many of genes found through our bioinformatic analysis to be significantly downregulated during chondrogenesis in multiple studies, and this included CAV1, FZD6, ITGA3, and MYH9.
evidence: This is based on SkeletalVis analysis comparing to other studies.

claim: Significant upregulation of FZD6, ITGA3, and CAV1 occurred after miR-199a-5p inhibition.
source: We saw significant upregulation of FZD6, ITGA3, and CAV1 after miR-199a-5p inhibition and miR-199a/b-5p inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A1.

claim: Significant upregulation of FZD6, ITGA3, and CAV1 occurred after miR-199a/b-5p inhibition.
source: We saw significant upregulation of FZD6, ITGA3, and CAV1 after miR-199a-5p inhibition and miR-199a/b-5p inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A1.

claim: There was no consistent improvement of the combination of miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p inhibition over miR-199a-5p inhibition alone.
source: There was no consistent improvement of the combination of miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p over miR-199a-5p alone.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data shown in Figure 4A1.

claim: CAV1 levels were significantly increased post miR-199b-5p inhibition.
source: We also tested the third most significant predicted target of miR-199a/b-5p – CAV1, and how its expression changed after miR-199b-5p inhibition over the same time course, and we saw CAV1 levels were significantly increased post miR-199b-5p inhibition (Lino Cardenas et al., 2013; Figure 4A2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A2.

claim: CAV1 has previously been established to be a direct target of miR-199a-5p.
source: Unlike FZD6 and ITGA3, CAV1 has previously been established to be a direct target of miR-199a-5p (Lino Cardenas et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lino Cardenas et al., 2013.

claim: FZD6 and ITGA3 3'UTRs contain potentially repressive elements.
source: To identify if FZD6 and ITGA3 were also direct miRNA targets, we cloned the 3′UTR regions of FZD6 and ITGA3 directly downstream of the firefly luciferase gene and demonstrated reduced expression compared to empty control vector, suggesting that these contain potentially repressive elements (Figure 4B1).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4B1.

claim: Introduction of an excess of miR-199a-5p into cells further repressed FZD6 and ITGA3 3'UTR luciferase expression, suggesting that both FZD6 and ITGA3 3'UTRs are direct miR-199a-5p targets.
source: Introduction of an excess of miR-199a-5p into the cells further repressed expression, suggesting that both FZD6 and ITGA3 3'UTRs are direct miR-199a-5p targets.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4B1.

claim: Mutation of the predicted miR-199-5p seed sequence within the 3′UTR of FZD6 and ITGA3 reduced the extent of inhibition of luciferase levels caused by the miRNA.
source: This was confirmed by mutation of the predicted miR-199-5p seed sequence within the 3′UTR of each gene which reduced the extent of inhibition of luciferase levels caused by the miRNA (Figure 4B2).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4B2.

claim: In the initial model, 15/18 modelled objects with experimental data had a mean squared error of lower than 3.
source: In the initial model, 15/18 modelled objects with experimental data had an MSE of lower than 3, indicating that most of the experimental data was captured by the model, and the average MSE for the model was 15.96.
evidence: This is based on comparison of model simulations to experimental data.

claim: The average mean squared error for the initial model was 15.96.
source: In the initial model, 15/18 modelled objects with experimental data had an MSE of lower than 3, indicating that most of the experimental data was captured by the model, and the average MSE for the model was 15.96.
evidence: This is based on comparison of model simulations to experimental data.

claim: In the enhanced model, 14/18 (77.7%) of the objects with experimental data had a mean squared error of >3.
source: In the enhanced model, 14/18 (77.7%) of the objects with experimental data had an MSE of >3, indicating the model – even with additional data from the literature – still captured much of the experimental data.
evidence: This is based on comparison of model simulations to experimental data.

claim: The average mean squared error for the enhanced model was 12.08.
source: Also, the average MSE was 12.08, indicating an improvement over the initial model.
evidence: This is based on comparison of model simulations to experimental data.

claim: The MIR199 family were identified as pro-chondrogenic in mouse mesenchymal C3H10T1/2 cells, reportedly by targeting SMAD1 (miR-199a-3p) and JAG1 (miR-199a/b-5p).
source: The MIR199 family were identified as pro-chondrogenic in mouse mesenchymal C3H10T1/2 cells, reportedly by targeting SMAD1 (miR-199a-3p) and JAG1 (miR-199a/b-5p), respectively (Zhang et al., 2020; Lin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2020 and Lin et al., 2009.

claim: miR-199a/b-5p promotes SOX9, COL2A1, and ACAN expression in human MSC chondrogenesis, thus enhancing cartilage formation.
source: Having previously shown the substantial upregulation of miR-199a/b-5p during chondrogenesis, we now show through both loss- and gain-of-function experiments that miR-199a/b-5p also promotes SOX9, COL2A1, and ACAN expression in human MSC chondrogenesis, thus enhancing cartilage formation (Barter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and cited work from Barter et al., 2015.

claim: miR-199a and miR-199b are vertebrate-specific miRNAs which exhibit an expression pattern associated with mesenchymal tissues and the skeleton.
source: miR-199a and miR-199b are vertebrate-specific miRNAs which exhibit an expression pattern associated with mesenchymal tissues and the skeleton (Desvignes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Desvignes et al., 2014.

claim: Antisense transcript Dmn3os encodes miR-199a and miR214 and its deletion in mice causes skeletal defects including short stature and cranial deformity.
source: Antisense transcript Dmn3os encodes miR-199a and miR214 and its deletion in mice causes skeletal defects including short stature and cranial deformity (Watanabe et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Watanabe et al., 2008.

claim: Similar phenotypic consequences caused by the loss of DNM3OS and therefore MIR199A and MIR214 have been reported in humans.
source: Similar phenotypic consequences caused by the loss of DNM3OS and therefore MIR199A and MIR214 have also been reported in humans (Lefroy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lefroy et al., 2018.

claim: miR-214 has been reported to negatively impact on chondrocyte differentiation, through targeting ATF4.
source: miR-214 has since been reported to negatively impact on chondrocyte differentiation, through targeting ATF4 (Roberto et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Roberto et al., 2018.

claim: TGFB triggers phosphorylation of CAV1 via SRC-kinase.
source: Several mechanisms reported in the literature may also support how miR-199a/b-5p-CAV1 could regulate chondrogenesis, such as TGFB triggering phosphorylation of CAV1 via SRC-kinase (Lino Cardenas et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lino Cardenas et al., 2013.

claim: miR-199a-5p-FZD6 interaction has been predicted previously.
source: In contrast to CAV1, FZD6 and ITGA3 have been less well studied as miR-199a/b-5p targets though, miR-199a-5p-FZD6 has been predicted previously (Lin et al., 2009; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2009 and Kim et al., 2015.

claim: Previous work by the authors has validated FZD6 as a target of miR-140-5p.
source: Previous work by our group has validated FZD6 as a target of miR-140-5p, so it is likely a highly important gene in chondrogenesis.
evidence: This refers to previous work by the authors' group.

claim: FZD6 is likely a highly important gene in chondrogenesis.
source: Previous work by our group has validated FZD6 as a target of miR-140-5p, so it is likely a highly important gene in chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that FZD6 is targeted by multiple pro-chondrogenic miRNAs.

claim: ITGA3 has been found to be a target of miR-199a-5p in neck and head cancer cells.
source: ITGA3 meanwhile has been found to be a target of miR-199a-5p in neck and head cancer cells, and our results confirm this interaction in humans MSCs (Tian et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tian et al., 2020.

claim: The results confirm the miR-199a-5p-ITGA3 interaction in human MSCs.
source: ITGA3 meanwhile has been found to be a target of miR-199a-5p in neck and head cancer cells, and our results confirm this interaction in humans MSCs (Tian et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: TGFB3 was used to initiate chondrogenesis in the experiments.
source: The enhanced chondrogenesis model (Figure 5C) was initiated with TGFB3, which was used to initiate chondrogenesis in our experiments and was therefore used as the proxy for chondrogenic initiation.
evidence: This is stated in the methods and model description.

claim: TGFB3 promoted miR-199a/b-5p levels to match microarray data.
source: As such, TGFB3 promoted miR-199a/b-5p levels to match our microarray data, though based on our previous data TGFB may not directly regulate miR-199a/b-5p levels (Barter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on the model design to match experimental data.

claim: Based on previous data TGFB may not directly regulate miR-199a/b-5p levels.
source: As such, TGFB3 promoted miR-199a/b-5p levels to match our microarray data, though based on our previous data TGFB may not directly regulate miR-199a/b-5p levels (Barter et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Barter et al., 2015.

claim: TGFB3 induced CAV1 via SRC kinase.
source: TGFB3 also induced CAV1 via SRC kinase and induced SOX9 via the SMAD2-SMAD3 pathway, which then stimulated SOX9 protein production (SMAD2/3 were not included in the models) (Coricor and Serra, 2016; Peng et al., 2008; Mishra et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on literature citations to Coricor and Serra, 2016; Peng et al., 2008; Mishra et al., 2007.

claim: TGFB3 induced SOX9 via the SMAD2-SMAD3 pathway, which then stimulated SOX9 protein production.
source: TGFB3 also induced CAV1 via SRC kinase and induced SOX9 via the SMAD2-SMAD3 pathway, which then stimulated SOX9 protein production (SMAD2/3 were not included in the models) (Coricor and Serra, 2016; Peng et al., 2008; Mishra et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on literature citations to Coricor and Serra, 2016; Peng et al., 2008; Mishra et al., 2007.

claim: Microarray data showed CAV1 gene expression decreased during early chondrogenesis, but then increased again.
source: However, our microarray data showed CAV1 gene expression decreased during early chondrogenesis, but then increased again – perhaps indicating CAV1 has a smaller negative regulative effect on chondrogenesis, or only effects early chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is based on microarray data from Barter et al., 2015.

claim: CAV1 may have a smaller negative regulative effect on chondrogenesis, or only effects early chondrogenesis.
source: However, our microarray data showed CAV1 gene expression decreased during early chondrogenesis, but then increased again – perhaps indicating CAV1 has a smaller negative regulative effect on chondrogenesis, or only effects early chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observed expression pattern of CAV1.

claim: FZD6 was negatively regulated by miR-140-5p in the model.
source: Gene expression of FZD6, ITGA3, CAV1 and the OtherTargets blackbox all had inverse relationships with miR-199a-5p and miR-199b-5p, and FZD6 was also negatively regulated by miR-140-5p.
evidence: This is based on the model design incorporating literature data.

claim: P-SOX9 promoted COL2A1, ACAN, and miR-140-5p expression in the model.
source: P-SOX9 promoted COL2A1, ACAN, and miR-140-5p expression.
evidence: This is based on the model design.

claim: Most cartilage GAGs are post-translationally added to Aggrecan, the protein product of ACAN.
source: ACAN contributed directly, and to the greatest extent, to GAG levels (since most cartilage GAGs are post-translationally added to Aggrecan, the protein product of ACAN) which was used as the phenotypic level output for the model and a proxy for chondrogenesis progression (Barter et al., 2015; Roughley and Mort, 2014; Hardingham and Fosang, 1992; Huang et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Barter et al., 2015; Roughley and Mort, 2014; Hardingham and Fosang, 1992; Huang et al., 2000.
